prompt_en: A sports photograph captures a sport participant during physical sporting effort. A woman riding a road bicycle is nearing the crest of a steep, quiet coastal road, still seated as she drives the near pedal downward. Use the supplied portrait as the reference for her facial appearance and short dark bob, with the same soft facial proportions and wispy fringe visible beneath a fitted cycling helmet. Her concentrated eyes stay on the road just beyond the crest; slightly parted lips and a faint, unposed release in her expression make the effort feel personal. Her navy cycling jersey and dark bib shorts follow the bent body naturally, with small creases at the elbows and hips. Both hands close around the two brake hoods, elbows flexed, torso reaching forward from the saddle; each shoe stays joined to its own pedal, the descending near leg and rising far knee forming one readable pedaling cycle. On the camera-near control, the heel of her palm bears on its black rubber hood, her fingers wrapping that same hood with the index finger lying beside the separate curved brake lever. That lever blade has a clear edge in front of the hood and extends downward toward the curved drop of the bar. A small dark cage is attached along the down tube inside the bicycle's open frame triangle. One pale blue cycling bottle sits with its lower body enclosed by this cage; its narrow neck and capped top project above the cage as separate forms against the open triangle. The two narrow tires meet the uphill tarmac, and the road continues visibly beneath and behind the bicycle. Photograph from the roadside ahead and to her left, close enough for her face to carry the image while including the entire bicycle and both tire contact points with room around them. Let the near control and the open frame triangle lie on the exposed side of the rider, with enough separation to read the lever edge and cage opening in the same view. The pale sea appears beyond a low roadside wall; the uphill edge line leads toward the brighter open road ahead. Early morning side light catches fine sweat at her temples and gives her cheek and forearm a quiet warmth. Keep the face, hands and bicycle contact geometry crisp, with the distant coast softly separated; the frame feels like an observed final push rather than a demonstration of technique.
